title: Oxytocin may be useful to increase trust in others and decrease disruptive behaviours in patients with Prader-Willi syndrome: a randomised placebo-controlled trial in 24 patients

what_it_measured.text: Oxytocin may be useful to increase trust in others and decrease disruptive behaviours in patients with Prader-Willi syndrome: a randomised placebo-controlled trial in 24 patients

dose.text: Methods: In a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study, 24 adult patients with PWS received a single intranasal administration of 24 IU of OT or placebo and were tested 45 min later on social skills.

route.text: Methods: In a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study, 24 adult patients with PWS received a single intranasal administration of 24 IU of OT or placebo and were tested 45 min later on social skills.

endpoint.text: The following were evaluated: amount of food intake per meal, amount of food requested per meal, duration of meal, and behaviour before/during/after the meal.
Each pair of patients of the same gender and same IQ range was evaluated the same day.

reported_results.text: In the half-day following administration, we observed a trend towards less conflict with others (p = 0.07) in the OT group compared with the placebo group.

Results: Patients with PWS who received a single intranasal administration of OT displayed significantly increased trust in others (P = 0.02) and decreased sadness tendencies (P = 0.02) with less disruptive behaviour (P = 0.03) in the two days following administration than did patients who received placebo.
There was no significant difference in the total RMET score between the two groups: 7 (4-9) in the OT group vs. 5.5 (1-11) (P = 0.18).
There was a trend (P = 0.07) towards a different evolution in the pre-post difference between the two groups for the disruptive behaviour item.
